content: Top 5 Tools and Software Every Fashion Designer Should Learn in 2026 Fashion design is evolving fast. From modern technologies to Indian designers crafting for global celebrities, the industry is transforming fast. Today’s fashion brands use digital tools, AI-powered software, virtual fashion technology, and 3D simulations to develop faster, smarter, and more eco-friendly designs. This evolution makes the Bachelor of Fashion Design from top private universities like Bennett University a smart academic move to build a thriving fashion design career. In today’s article, we will explore the top 5 tools that every fashion design student must know and apply to their projects and future workplaces. content: UNION EDUCATION ELIGIBILITY  Should be an Indian national  For studies in India  Secured admission to an eligible course in a recognized institution in India.  Minimum marks secured in qualifying exam should be as under: Category Minimum marks General 60% OBC 55% SC/ST 50%  Qualifying exam is defined as any examination/course which is a prerequisite for securing admission to the proposed course of study. Example: 10+2/higher secondary exam is a qualifying exam for securing admission to Degree course  Note: Wherever grades are given instead of marks in the qualifying exams, then the grades corresponding to the above-mentioned marks should be considered.  There is no restriction with regard to the minimum and maximum age of the student to be eligible for the education loan.  If the student is minor, the parent/guardian has to execute the documents. After the students attains the age of majority, branch should obtain a letter of ratification from the student. ELIGIBLE CO-APPLICANTS  The parent(s) of the student has to compulsorily join in as co-applicant.  In case of a married person, co-applicant can be spouse/parent(s)/parent(s)-in-law.  Further, in cases where both the parents are not alive, close relative or guardian to be taken as co-applicant.  The co-applicant should be Indian national. ELIGIBILE COURSES  Courses eligible for loan are the ones taken up after completion of higher secondary school, i.e. 10 + 2 stage or equivalent  Studies in India:  Approved courses leading to graduate/post graduate degree or post graduate diploma conducted by recognized colleges/ universities recognized by UGC/ Govt. / AICTE/ AIBMS/ ICMR etc  Courses like ICWA, CA, CFA etc  Courses conducted by IIMs, IITs, IISc, XLRI, NIFT, NID etc  Regular degree/ diploma courses like Aeronautical, pilot training, shipping etc., approved by Director General of Civil Aviation/ Shipping, if the course is pursued in India  Approved courses offered in India by reputed foreign universities  Students seeking admission through management quota will be considered under the regular scheme.  Reference: www.ugc.ac.in, www.education.nic.in, www.aicte.org.in,

content: universities  Students seeking admission through management quota will be considered under the regular scheme.  Reference: www.ugc.ac.in, www.education.nic.in, www.aicte.org.in, www.naac.gov.in/Universities_Colleges.asp,www.iba.org.in/Documents/Agrade institutions.pdf QUANTUM  Need based finance to meet the expenses will be considered taking into account margins norms.  There will be no maximum amount of loan that can be sanctioned under the education loan scheme. Amount to be sanctioned as per delegation of the respective sanctioning authority MARGIN Quantum of loan Margin Up to Rs.4 Lakh Nil Above Rs.4 Lakh 5%  Scholarship / assistance to be included in margin  Margin may be brought in on year-to-year basis as and when disbursement is made on a pro-rata basis REPAYMENT TENURE  Maximum repayment tenure will be 15 years ( After course & moratorium period) irrespective of quantum of loan.  Loan to be repaid by way of EMI.  The accrued interest during the moratorium period ( if nor Served) the be added to the principal amount while calculating EMI for repayment. RATE OF INTEREST  As per rate card (presently EBLR + 2.10% for Male, EBLR + 1.60% for Female students for loan above ₹ 7.50 lakhs). Current EBLR is 9.30% (applicable from 01-04- 2023)  Simple interest to be charged during the course/moratorium period.  Compounding rate of interest to be charged after course/moratorium period. Branches should note and feed in the system the actual date of commencement of repayment so that correct interest is charged in the loan account. INTEREST REBATE  If interest is regularly serviced during the course and moratorium period, i.e. prior to the commencement of repayment, then the student is eligible for interest rebate.  Rebate of 1% to be given in the applicable rate of interest for the repayment period only, i.e. the period commencing after course and moratorium period. For Details Please contact Alok Jaiswal on 9810221445 or alokjaiswal@unionbankofindia.bank
